questions: How many oxidized or etched CsV3Sb5 devices did you make, and how many showed a diode? You list ten pristine devices (Table S1), four diode-active ones (Devices 11 to 14) and two Ti-doped ones (Devices 15 and 16); the total processed count and the number of cooldowns would complete the picture.
Why were any others set aside, and why is Device 1, the device of Fig. 1, absent from Table S1?

Which ranges did you measure beyond those shown: how many zero-field sweeps per device in total, which sweep rates for Devices 11 to 13, temperatures above 1.5 K for Device 13, and fields between 0 and 0.1 T?

What does the second-best dataset look like, for example the zero-field η distribution of Device 14 with as many sweeps as Fig. 3, and of Devices 11 and 12 at each oxidation step? Fig. S3's caption calls Device 12 "Fig. 2 in the main text", which shows Device 11, and Fig. S4 is titled Device 13 while carrying the Device 12 values quoted on p. 5; which device is in each figure?

What is the residual field at the sample when the magnet reads zero, in the PPMS and in the Triton, and was the magnet reset before the zero-field sweeps? When you step the field through zero in fine steps, where does the mean η cross zero?

Each sweep in Fig. 2 runs to ±300 μA, far above Ic. Does the η distribution change if sweeps stop just above Ic, or if you warm above Tc between sweeps, and does field-cooling at +1 T and at −1 T (Fig. S8) give opposite zero-field signs?

For Fig. 3d,e and Fig. 4, what is the mean signed η at zero field with its standard error, and what do the |Ic+| and |Ic−| histograms look like separately? How is the onset picked when dV/dI has several peaks, and how does the 10 μA ac excitation labeled in Fig. S3 compare with the 16.8 to 36 μA critical currents in Fig. S4?
For the Ti-doped Devices 15 and 16, what are the thickness, Tc and Ic, how many sweeps went into Figs. S13 and S14, and did oxidation produce the same multi-peak transition as in Device 11?
